page: Google Cloud Platform m4n-hypermem-64 is an x86_64 server instance provisioned with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 992 GB of system memory. Classified under the Network Optimized server family, the instance offers an expansive memory footprint delivering 15.5 GB of RAM per vCPU core. The platform features no integrated GPUs and includes no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for persistent data. Additionally, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

With 992 GB of memory mapped to 64 dedicated compute cores, the machine is structured for workloads bounded by memory capacity rather than raw compute scaling. The absence of local disk requires external volume attachments, separating compute and storage tiers over the network. From an infrastructure cost perspective, the 15.5 GB-per-core ratio allows organizations to satisfy extreme memory requirements without overpaying for unnecessary processor capacity. This balance fits large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise caching systems, real-time analytics engines, and high-footprint transactional processing.
description: Google Cloud Platform m4n-hypermem-64 is a high-memory server instance built on the x86_64 architecture, featuring 64 dedicated vCPUs and 992 GB of total system RAM. Positioned within the Network Optimized family, this configuration delivers a high memory-to-core allocation of 15.5 GB per vCPU. The machine includes no hardware accelerators and provides no bundled local storage, necessitating external network storage volumes for file and operating system data. In terms of resource allocation, the high RAM density ensures cost efficiency for software platforms that demand expansive memory working sets without requiring excess compute provisioning. The instance is suited for running large-scale in-memory databases, real-time streaming architectures, high-capacity enterprise caching systems, and distributed memory-bound analytics.
